messages:
harper: Quick handoff from my shift — FYI saw elevated tail latency for KV cache (us-east Redis cluster) between ~02:05–03:25 UTC. No 5xx spike, just p95 jump and increased queueing. I toggled a few runtime fallbacks (reduced batch size on low-priority routes, enabled prefix caching) which brought p95 down ~20%. Leaving notes and a couple questions below. cc @sam @maya

sam: Thanks for the writeup. Good call on runtime mitigations. Quick clarification on ownership we should standardize: SRE owns the infra layer (Redis, autoscaling, network, node OOMs). Runtime owns model-serving controls (batching, fallbacks, route pinning, KV cache usage). If something causes customer-facing errors (increased 5xx or SLO breaches) -> declare an incident and page oncall-sre immediately. Otherwise treat as operational degradation and follow the mitigation steps you did. :thumbsup:

maya: Adding nuance from runtime side — for degradations that are latency-only (p95/p99), runtime should be first line: we can apply conservative fallbacks fast (smaller batch, pin to cheaper model variant, enable KV prefills). If diagnostics show Redis timeouts or server-level metrics spiking, escalate to SRE. For private deployments, runtime still handles model fallbacks but involve the customer's infra lead + support early.

lee: One practical ask — do we have a short paging matrix we can paste in the runbook? Right now folks ping either team and it creates noise. Also, for post-shift follow-ups who files the follow-up? The last time it fell between teams.

sam: Good point. Suggested quick matrix (we should add to runbook):

```
IF -> symptom -> who to page / notify
------------------------------------------------
customer-facing errors (5xx spike, high error rate) -> page oncall-sre -> escalate to SRE lead
latency-only (p95 up, no 5xx) -> page runtime-oncall -> runtime applies fallbacks
infra alarms (Redis timeouts, node OOM, network flaps) -> page oncall-sre -> SRE triages
private-deploy customer-impact -> page customer-success + runtime + SRE (if infra)
```

sam: For follow-ups: whoever applies the mitigation should create a short follow-up note in the incident-notes doc if it crossed a threshold (SLO or customer impact). If it was purely runtime mitigation with no customer impact, runtime-oncall files a 1-paragraph post-shift note and assigns an owner for any follow-ups.

maya: I'll open a tiny playbook PR with the matrix and the quick checklist (who pages, what logs to attach, minimal triage steps). Assigning to @natalie for runbook merge if that's okay.

natalie: happy to merge — please add 2 lines on who to CC for private deploys (security and account lead). Also include a pointer to the alert dashboards and the runbook fragment: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/oncall-escalation (linked)

harper: Thanks all. Action items for me: paste my diagnostic snippet and latency graphs to the follow-up note, mark owner for deeper Redis investigation if we see recurrence. FYI I captured the commands I ran:

```
# reduced batch size for low-priority route
POST /admin/runtime-config
{ "route": "/search/low", "batch_size": 8 }

# enabled prefix caching for /chat-stream
POST /admin/cache/toggle
{ "route": "/chat-stream", "state": "on", "ttl": 60 }
```

oncall-bot: Rotation reminder — runtime-oncall: maya (this week). SRE oncall: sam. :bell:

lee: Perfect, thanks. If no objections I'll link the new PR in the runbook and close out the follow-up tomorrow morning.

harper: No objections. Thanks everyone — feel free to @me if anything else pops up during the day.
